sources.title: T. H. Nguyen, Notes on Recent Work on the Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture
sources.locator: §1, PDF pp. 2–5 (Theorems 1.3–1.4 and Lemmas 1.5–1.7); §2, PDF pp. 7–8 (Lemmas 13–15 and Theorem 16)

contents.name: Lemma 1.7
contents.reason: This is the flexible f-EH amplification used to reprove approximate general bounds; the page only needs the constant-exponent case, and no later planned page in the current run owns the broader f-parameter formulation as a standalone result.

contents.name: Lemma 15
contents.reason: This is the closeness-to-a-hereditary-class analogue used for the polynomial close Rödl property; the current page is about restricted sets forced by forbidden induced copies, not by edit distance to a hereditary class, and no page in the active plan isolates the close-Rödl variant.

sources.title: M. Bucić, J. Fox, and H. T. Pham, Equivalence between Erdős-Hajnal and polynomial Rödl and Nikiforov conjectures
sources.locator: §1 Introduction and §2 Proofs in full, arXiv HTML lines 29–175

contents.name: Proposition 6
contents.reason: The sharpness example is specific to P4 and to the near-tight quantitative constant in Theorem 5. This page proves only the qualitative equivalence, so the sharpness construction would be a side theorem with no later consumer in the plan.

contents.name: Theorem 7
contents.reason: The hereditary-family theorem is broader than the finite-family formulation this page needs, and writing it honestly would require a second definition of the polynomial Rödl property for an arbitrary hereditary class. The finite-family equivalence already captures the theorem used later in the Erdős–Hajnal block.

contents.name: Corollary 8
contents.reason: String graphs are not yet constructed anywhere in the library, and this corollary is a subject-specific application whose statement would import an unbuilt graph class only to illustrate an implication already proved abstractly here.

contents.name: Corollary 9
contents.reason: Perfect graphs and their sharp polynomial Rödl bound belong to the later perfect-pattern development, not to this equivalence page. The result is an application of the equivalence rather than part of its proof spine.

contents.name: Conjecture 10
contents.reason: The polynomial close Rödl property is a different strengthening involving edit distance to a hereditary family, not forbidden-copy counts. No current page in the active plan owns this edit-distance variant or its applications.

contents.name: Theorem 11
contents.reason: The close-Rödl equivalence is outside the current page remit, which is the restricted-set and forbidden-copy equivalence used later in the Erdős–Hajnal block; the library has not developed graph edit distance as a recurring notion here.

contents.name: Lemma 15
contents.reason: The closeness lemma serves the polynomial close Rödl theorem rather than the viral equivalence. It would introduce graph-edit witnesses with no other consumer on this page or in its declared prerequisites.

sources.title: S. Huang, Y. Ju, and Y. Zhou, Erdős-Hajnal beyond the five-vertex path
